title: My Aunt Has A Key To YOURS
premise: My aunt Lou, the court's locksmith, has a key to every house on our court and locks them all at midnight, except mine, which never clicks, and my sneakers are wet every morning.
twist: The one walking the court at midnight is me, asleep, trying handles on my way home to her house, so she races round locking every door but hers to make sure the only one I can open is hers; I stop sleepwalking when I walk over to her table awake.
world: A horseshoe court of twelve narrow red-brick houses round a stone fountain, painted doors in a row of colours, a steady brass carriage lamp on every door; Aunt Lou's teal door with a brass knocker, red geraniums and a striped mat, and her warm kitchen.
